steps.title: Create the Slack App
steps.detail: Go to the Slack API Portal (https://api.slack.com/apps), click 'Create New App', choose 'From scratch' or a manifest, name the app, and select your dev workspace.

evidence.note: App creation steps are documented in Slack's OAuth installation guide.

steps.title: Configure Scopes
steps.detail: Navigate to Features > OAuth & Permissions, and add required Bot Token Scopes (e.g. chat:write) and/or User Token Scopes.
steps.notes: Can be defined via an app manifest file that an agent writes.

evidence.note: Scope configurations are managed under OAuth & Permissions.

verification.note: Configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs
steps.detail: Under Redirect URLs in the OAuth & Permissions page, add your application's HTTPS callback URI and save changes.
steps.notes: Developer must specify exact URIs matching application code.

evidence.note: Redirect URIs must be explicitly configured.

verification.note: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS. Alternatively, you can configure a Redirect URL in the App Management page under OAuth & Permissions

pitfalls.description: Combining Sign in with Slack (SIWS) OpenID user scopes with non-SIWS scopes in a single authorization URL redirect causes an error.

evidence.note: Docs state SIWS and standard scopes must be requested in separate flows.

verification.note: A scope conflict occurs when attempting to combine Sign in with Slack (SIWS) user scopes with non-Sign in with Slack scopes

pitfalls.description: Failing to explicitly pass the exact redirect_uri parameter in both the authorize and token exchange steps causes a bad_redirect_uri error when multiple URIs are configured.

evidence.note: Redirect URI matching pitfall documented in the OAuth guide.

verification.note: When there are multiple Redirect URL values configured, the redirect_url parameter must be sent in both the Authorize and Access steps... otherwise, you will encounter a bad_redirect_uri error

pitfalls.description: Reinstalling an app with a subset of previously granted scopes does not remove the old scopes; permissions are strictly additive unless the token is fully revoked.

evidence.note: Additive scope behaviors are documented in the installation guide.

verification.note: both channels:history and channels:read will be assigned to the token. There is no way to remove scopes from an existing token without revoking it entirely.

probes.summary: OpenID Connect discovery document found (issuer: https://slack.com).
No RFC 8414 authorization server metadata at 2 candidate location(s).
Authorization endpoint (from docs) responds to a request with a fake client_id (HTTP 200); response mentions an OAuth/client error.
Token endpoint (from docs) is live: an unauthenticated request with a fake code returned OAuth error "invalid_code" (HTTP 200).
Discovery metadata does not advertise a registration_endpoint, so dynamic client registration is likely unsupported.
Metadata does not list code_challenge_methods_supported (PKCE may still be supported; check docs).

limitations: No accounts were created, no forms submitted, no OAuth apps registered, and no credentials were used. Probes are unauthenticated GET requests against public discovery documents, endpoints and documentation pages, plus one unauthenticated POST to the token endpoint with a fake authorization code and a nonexistent client_id (to confirm it answers with an OAuth error).
